scope: Investigate generated DWG LTYPE_CONTROL order, ownership roles and resulting linetype semantics. The proposed change was reverted; this receipt does not qualify the route or authorize a broader support claim.
authority: ODA Open Design Specification v5.4.1 section 20.4.57 says the entry count excludes BYBLOCK/BYLAYER, ordinary entries are soft owners, and the two special entries are hard owners. Its stated order is linetypes ending with BYLAYER and BYBLOCK. The repository instruction makes this PDF authoritative for DWG layout conflicts.

source.provenance: An ezdxf 1.4.5 R2010 DXF was authored from scratch with CONTINUOUS and USER_DASH, a DASH_LAYER, and default/custom LINEs. ODA File Converter 27.1.0 converted it independently to six versions; GNU LibreDWG 0.14 decoded each control. Reproduce with tools/audit_dwg_ltype_control.py. No drawing fixtures are committed.
source.observed: In each source LibreDWG reports ordinary role-2 CONTINUOUS and USER_DASH references, then role-3 ByBlock and role-3 ByLayer. This observed order conflicts with the stated BYLAYER/BYBLOCK order in the authoritative ODA specification. The custom layer and explicit LINE resolve to USER_DASH in the peer decoder.

problem: The current writer places ByBlock and ByLayer before ordinary entries and marks every child role 2, while the count excludes the two special records. A locally generated AC1024 material/plotstyle output was decoded as entries=[ByBlock], byblock=ByLayer, bylayer=Continuous; ODA exported its default BYLAYER LINE as ByBlock. This exposes a real consumer-visible linetype risk.

reverted_experiment.change: A scratch candidate put ordinary entries first, then ByBlock and ByLayer as hard owners. The ordering contradicts the authoritative specification and was removed from production code and test integration.
reverted_experiment.wire_checks: Locally generated candidate frames passed CRC, entry-count, handle-role and following-record checks for AC1015/18/24/27/32; LibreDWG decoded their custom linetype references. Native six-version readback and invalid-write rollback/retry also passed. These results only describe the reverted candidate.
reverted_experiment.oda_default_control: Scratch candidate AC1024 DWG SHA-256 84b562c69091348ac3961863e57032d6b3ebf128fe91f8854e3d807c3a32e483 converted to DXF SHA-256 9c3e2f64e0f1f52dc7ea91403a673efa3f861743c4c572037b27820fa5e23241 without .err; ezdxf reported CONTINUOUS on layer 0 and BYLAYER/BYBLOCK on the two LINEs. This observed consumer result does not override the PDF.
reverted_experiment.oda_limits: A separate generated custom-layer candidate failed at its caller LAYER record; using synthetic layer 0 advanced that candidate to an error at its caller USER_DASH LTYPE record. No ODA custom-linetype or custom-layer semantic claim follows.

count_encoding: ODA section 20.4.57 specifies the LTYPE_CONTROL entry count as BL, whereas the current reader and writer use BS. The six source controls contain only two ordinary entries, whose BS and BL encodings coincide, so they do not resolve this discrepancy. Independent producer-authored 255/256/257-entry controls with exact following fields, boundary and reader compatibility are needed before any count-layout change.
ac1021: A separate pre-existing R2007 framing issue prevents LibreDWG decoding the generated LTYPE_CONTROL handle stream. The producer source still decodes correctly. Do not conflate that issue with the special-record order conflict.
next_steps: Obtain an authoritative ODA correction, clarification, or specimen whose raw handle spans and special-record names resolve the BYLAYER/BYBLOCK discrepancy; do not choose the contradictory producer interpretation solely from peer-reader or ODA converter behavior.

Generate and independently decode 255/256/257 ordinary-entry producer controls and inspect their physical count and following fields against ODA BL; separately design strict historical BS-output compatibility before touching count encoding.

After resolving order, stage ordinary entries and special roles with exact count, boundary, CRC and following-field controls. Verify caller linetypes, native readback, independent ODA semantics, destination preservation, corrected retry and ABI compatibility.

Treat strict fail-closed output as a separate bounded opt-in or qualification decision; globally refusing routine built-in linetypes would break broad existing consumers. Until then leave existing default behavior unchanged and do not promote this output profile.
Investigate AC1021's object-size/string/handle boundary independently, preserving explicitly identified historical malformed output only through a narrowly validated reader fallback.
